text: When combining whole-cell submodels built by different research groups, which standard is specifically designed to represent ODE- and stochastic-reaction-network models in an exchangeable format?
choices: BioPAX (Biological Pathway Exchange), an OWL-based format used primarily to link pathway components to biological databases
SBO (Systems Biology Ontology), a controlled vocabulary of terms for annotating model elements
COBRAme, a Python framework specifically for constructing ME-models
explanation: SBML (Systems Biology Markup Language) is the standard file format for representing and exchanging ODE- and stochastic-reaction-network models, and it underlies curated repositories such as the BioModels Database. BioPAX (choice 0) serves a related but distinct purpose of linking pathway information to biological databases using an OWL-based ontology, and SBO (choice 2) provides standardized vocabulary terms rather than a model-exchange file format. COBRAme (choice 3) is a software framework for building a specific model type (ME-models), not a general semantic-alignment standard.
